newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate rises to 8.6 from 7.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate rises to 8.6 from 7.6 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate rose a whole percentage point to 8.6 percent on Wednesday, boosted by 15-30 day interbank borrowing at 11 percent in otherwise thin trade.
Settlements dwindled to 9.6 million kuna as few banks sought funds and only 7.5 million were new loans, Zagreb Money Market dealers said. Supply rose to 140 million.
Lenders kept their rates steady. Call money was unchanged at 8.0 percent and insurerance firms rolled over previous 10-15 day placements at 7.0 percent.
Tuesday's overnight trade left a huge surplus on the supply side after no more than 3.1 million kuna borrowings by four banks seeking to square their positions.

The National Bank of Croatia said it had no foreign exchange operations and planned none for some time. Its kuna midrates for Thursday eased to 5.3707 from 5.3478 to the dollar while firming marginally to 3.5533 against the German mark. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
